text.p: These are the leading stories in the Kenyan press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Uganda threatens to raise unilaterally tariffs charged on electricity sold to Kenya and says it expects to be paid at commercial rates.
- Public health personnel from the Nairobi City Council impounds expired powder milk worth millions of shillings.
- Opposition FORD-Kenya and Democratic parties reject a call by veteran politician John Keen for the extension of parliament by a year to allow for constitutional reform before the general election.
- Oil companies hike prices of petrol, kerosene and diesel by between 60 and 70 cents a litre -- the third price shock for petroleum products this year.
- Canned fish, baby food, condoms and confectionery products are impounded at a supermarket in Nairobi's Westlands suburb as their expiry date had expired.
- Unknown treasure hunters, allegedly hunting for colonial and post-independence coins, exhume the skeleton of a man buried eight years ago.
- The Kenya Bureau of Standards launches a new quality mark, replacing a previous mark which they say had become vulnerable to abuse by unscrupulous manufacturers.
- Market analysts call for a continued review of the Nairobi Stock Exchange 20-share index to make it a better reflector of market performance and increase investor confidence.
